title: A Portrait Made of Objects
fact_notes: 登場人物・出来事は架空の教材例。実在の調査結果ではない。リンクは制作台帳であり実証資料ではない。

sentences.en: An art teacher asked her students to create portraits of people they knew.
sentences.ja: 美術教師は知っている人の肖像画を作るよう求めた。

sentences.en: However, they were not allowed to draw anyone's face.
sentences.ja: しかし誰の顔も描いてはいけなかった。

sentences.en: Instead, they had to choose objects that represented the person.
sentences.ja: 代わりに人物を表す物を選ぶ必要があった。

sentences.en: Kenta decided to make a portrait of his grandfather.
sentences.ja: ケンタは祖父の肖像画を作ることにした。

sentences.en: His first drawing included a large fishing boat beside a blue sea.
sentences.ja: 最初の絵には青い海のそばに大きな漁船を描いた。

sentences.en: His grandfather had often taken him fishing when he was younger.
sentences.ja: 幼い頃、祖父はよく釣りに連れていってくれた。

sentences.en: Kenta also drew a clock, a cup, and a pair of gloves.
sentences.ja: 時計、カップ、手袋も描いた。

sentences.en: Yet the picture seemed more like a collection than a portrait.
sentences.ja: しかし絵は肖像画というより物を集めたように見えた。

sentences.en: His teacher asked him to explain why each object mattered.
sentences.ja: 教師はそれぞれの物がなぜ重要か説明するよう求めた。

sentences.en: Kenta described how his grandfather always repaired his old gloves.
sentences.ja: 祖父がいつも古い手袋を修理していたことを話した。

sentences.en: He remembered the many small repairs they had made together.
sentences.ja: 一緒に行った多くの小さな修理を思い出した。

sentences.en: He decided to place the gloves at the center of the picture.
sentences.ja: 手袋を絵の中央に置くことにした。

sentences.en: Next, he made the fishing boat smaller and removed the clock.
sentences.ja: 次に漁船を小さくし時計を取り除いた。

sentences.en: He added a needle and some thread beside the gloves.
sentences.ja: 手袋のそばに針と糸を加えた。

sentences.en: The finished work suggested patience and care without showing a person.
sentences.ja: 完成作品は人物を描かずに忍耐と思いやりを表した。

sentences.en: His classmates offered several different interpretations of the image.
sentences.ja: クラスメートは絵の異なる解釈をいくつか述べた。

sentences.en: Kenta understood that objects could express more than their practical purpose.
sentences.ja: 物は実用的な目的以上の意味を表せると理解した。

sentences.en: Their position and size could help guide a viewer's attention.
sentences.ja: 位置や大きさは見る人の注意を導ける。

sentences.en: A portrait did not necessarily need to reproduce someone's appearance.
sentences.ja: 肖像画は必ずしも人の外見を再現する必要はなかった。

sentences.en: It could communicate something about how that person lived.
sentences.ja: その人の生き方について何かを伝えられた。

vocabulary.definition: things that can be seen or touched
stood for a person or idea
a boat used for catching fish
things worn to protect the hands
a number of things brought together
made something work or usable again
a thin pointed tool used for sewing
a thin strand used for sewing
in a way that must be true
the way someone or something looks

questions.prompt: What were students not allowed to draw?
questions.explanation_ja: 顔を描いてはいけなかった。

questions.prompt: Why was fishing important to Kenta?
options: His grandfather had taken him fishing.
questions.explanation_ja: 祖父と釣りに行った思い出。

questions.prompt: Why was Kenta dissatisfied with his first picture?
options: He had used only red paint.
He had accidentally drawn a face.
The objects did not yet form a meaningful portrait.
questions.explanation_ja: 物を並べたように見えた。

questions.prompt: What did Kenta remember about the gloves?
options: They had been bought that morning.

questions.prompt: Where did he place the gloves?
How can an artist guide a viewer's attention?
options: By reproducing every object at the same size.
By using the position and size of objects.
By using a clock to limit viewing time.
Art should show only practical tools.
Objects in art can suggest a person's values and way of living.
All viewers interpret an image identically.
questions.explanation_ja: 物によって人物の生き方を表せる。
